project.name: GLib (staged ARVO checkout at f77c75a1bb37865348bd384bccea3d45f7da77c6)
project.commit_note: The staged ARVO workspace checkout at `/src/glib` is on commit `f77c75a1bb37865348bd384bccea3d45f7da77c6`, not the metadata `vulnerable_commit`. All line anchors below were resolved against that staged vulnerable tree, which still contains the unfixed `uri_decoder()` lookahead shown in `patch.diff`.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42485332 (glib): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target fuzz_uri_parse_params [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42485332
bug_description.normalized: In the staged GLib checkout `f77c75a1bb37865348bd384bccea3d45f7da77c6`, the exact 2-byte witness `3d 25` (`"=%"`) makes `g_uri_parse_params()` treat the whole buffer as one parameter, find `=` at byte 0, and pass the one-byte value substring `%` to `uri_decode()` with explicit `length == 1`. `uri_decoder()` then sets `end = start + 1`, sees `*s == '%'`, and evaluates `g_ascii_isxdigit(s[1]) || g_ascii_isxdigit(s[2])` without first checking that two lookahead bytes remain. The first lookahead `s[1]` lands exactly at the end of the 2-byte heap testcase allocation, producing the saved AddressSanitizer `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `uri_decoder -> uri_decode -> g_uri_parse_params`. The fix matches this exact obligation by adding `s + 2 >= end` before the hex-digit tests and adding regression cases for `%` and `=%`.

source.description: First project-side parse of the attacker-controlled params buffer into a parameter span. For the exact witness there is no `&`, so the whole 2-byte input becomes the first attr/value segment.
source.value_from: In `fuzzing/fuzz_uri_parse_params.c:13`, the harness calls `g_uri_parse_params ((const gchar *) data, (gssize) size, '&', FALSE)` on the exact 2-byte file `poc`, whose bytes are `3d 25` (`"=%"`). With `size == 2` and `separator == '&'`, this step searches that exact span for the only parameter boundary.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

tainted_value_origin.description: The parser materializes the trailing value subspan and its explicit length. For `"=%"`, `value` points at the final `%` byte and `value_end - value == 1`, which are the exact `start,length` arguments forwarded into `uri_decoder()`.
tainted_value_origin.note: Because the witness has `=` at byte 0 and no `&`, the attribute is empty and the value is the final byte.

root_cause.description: Missing truncated-escape guard. After entering the `%` branch, `uri_decoder()` tests `s[1]` and `s[2]` without first rejecting `s + 2 >= end`; the patch adds that precheck exactly.
root_cause.note: For this witness step 4 establishes `end == s + 1`, so the added `s + 2 >= end` rejection would fire before any lookahead.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The first hex-digit lookahead reads one byte past the one-byte value buffer passed to `uri_decoder()`.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at `glib/guri.c:256:16` in `uri_decoder`, with stack `uri_decode -> g_uri_parse_params -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`.

parser_admitted.code: parsed_params = g_uri_parse_params ((const gchar *) data, (gssize) size, '&', FALSE);
parser_admitted.description: Harness-only checkpoint. The staged 2-byte witness is passed unchanged into GLib's parameter parser with explicit `length == 2`.
parser_admitted.note: The preceding `if (size > G_MAXSSIZE)` check is not taken for the saved 2-byte PoC.

fine_trace.note: Source. The staged harness passes exact bytes `3d 25` (`"=%"`) with `length == 2` and `separator == '&'`. No `&` exists in that span, so the parser keeps the whole buffer as one parameter by setting `value_end = end = params + 2`.
The same 2-byte span contains `=` at the first byte, so `attr_end == params`. The early-return path for parameters without `=` is not taken.
Advancing past the `=` makes `value = params + 1`, which points to the trailing `%` byte, and `value_end - value == 1`. `g_uri_parse_params()` passes that exact 1-byte subspan into `uri_decode()`.

fine_trace.code: for (s = start, end = s + length, d = decoded; s < end; s++)
fine_trace.note: Inside `uri_decoder()`, the forwarded subspan becomes decoder bounds: `s == start == value`, `end = s + 1`, and the loop admits exactly the lone `%` byte.
The only byte in the 1-byte value buffer is `%`, so the percent-decoding branch is taken.

Root cause. This lookahead predicate assumes two bytes remain after `%`. For this witness step 4 established `end == s + 1`, so the missing precondition is the patch's `s + 2 >= end` rejection. Without that bound check, evaluating the hex-digit test dereferences past the explicit one-byte buffer.

Sink. `s[1]` is the first byte past the one-byte value buffer and therefore lands 0 bytes to the right of the 2-byte heap testcase allocation reported by ASan. The saved trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` at this statement.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports the invalid read is 0 bytes to the right of a 2-byte heap region allocated by the AFL/libFuzzer driver when it loaded the staged PoC.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42485332 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, which fed `poc` to `/out/fuzz_uri_parse_params` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `uri_decoder` with stack `uri_decode -> g_uri_parse_params`.

format.name: raw
format.contract: An exact 2-byte input `0x3d 0x25` (`"=%"`). Under the staged harness, `g_uri_parse_params (..., '&', FALSE)` parses this as an empty attribute plus a one-byte value `%`, so `uri_decoder()` receives `start = params + 1` and `length = 1` and the `%` lookahead reads `s[1]` past the explicit buffer end.
